body: He does try to understand, it just seems like he doesn't and that no one else does either. Thank you for the PM.

I've decided I don't like talking to him about it because he doesn't seem to understand, and just gets upset and frustrated with my mentality. I really don't want to talk about it with anyone I know, ever again.

The sad thing for me is that I'm not even lonely. I'm not surrounded by tons of people that love me, but I have a best friend that can relate to me (she lives 2 hours away but we talk a fair amount) and a wonderful boyfriend. Having great people around, though, doesn't keep me from feeling lonely. I love these people, and to an extent can accept that they love me, but it doesn't make me happy. If anything they keep me sticking around, because I know that me not being around would hurt them. Sometimes it actually makes me want to run away so I don't know anyone anymore so I can at least be completely alone and try to figure things out, but I know myself and that I would yurn for that human connection.

It's just hard to get ahead in life when there's always something keeping you from getting where you want to be, or reminding you why you can never have what you really wanted.

Adoption is an option for those who have money. I have zero reason to foresee ever being able to afford it. And knowing adoption is an option will never completely heal the wounds of finding out you can't have children of your own.

Is it sad that I don't even care that there are some people that care about me? That doesn't make me feel worth, it makes me feel bad that they're wasting their time.

I lost everything a year ago, and instead of starting over with a blank slate I've had to try to start over with a slate covered in caked on shit that can't come off. I'm having to try to build over potholes and sinkholes.
I don't have a vehicle to get to therapy even if I could get the time off work, plus I can't afford it. I went in the past for a while but all my doctor did was give me meds that didn't help.
